Read the values and copy them out. Rules: 1. Only copy the numbers you can see clearly. Don’t guess, don’t calculate, don’t convert anything. 2. If a value doesn’t appear anywhere, or if you have any doubt, don’t write its line. 3. Reply ONLY with the blocks below: no text before, after or between them, no explanation. 4. One line per value, in the format key: number, with a period for decimals. Keep the key names exactly as they are. No units, except for a mass in pounds or stones (write lb or st after the number, example: poids_kg: 12 st 4 lb) and for a length in inches (write in after the number). 5. One block per date, from YOROI BALANCE v1 to FIN. Everything measured on the same day goes into a single block, even if it comes from several photos (the scale in the morning, the tape measure in the evening). Photos arrive in any order and may repeat: a value seen on two photos is written only once. 6. The date of each block: look for it in this order. The date shown on the scale screen or in the app screenshot (date_source: ecran). The date printed on a receipt or sheet (date_source: ticket). Otherwise the date the photo was taken, if you have access to it or if it’s in the list “Photo capture dates” at the end of this message (date_source: photo). Write it in the format date: YYYY-MM-DD, and on the next line where it comes from: date_source: ecran, ticket or photo. If the day and month are visible but not the year, write date: DD/MM, the app will add the year. If you can’t find any date, write date: inconnue and date_source: inconnue, the app will ask for the day. A date visible on the photo always wins over the capture date. Never make up a date, don’t use the file date or the sending date, never today’s date. 7. App history or chart: each row showing a written date and number becomes a block at its date. Don’t read a value from the height of a curve, only written numbers. A weekly or monthly average is not a weigh-in: don’t write it. 8. Many scales (Tanita included) don’t write the name of the measurement: recognize it by its unit, its small symbol and its value range. kg with the standing figure, largest value: poids_kg. kg with the muscular figure (dumbbell), about 30 to 90: muscle_kg. Small kg, about 1 to 6, with the bone symbol: os_kg. % with the figure and the % symbol, about 3 to 50: graisse_pct. % with the water drop, about 35 to 75: eau_pct. Level: graisse_viscerale. Age: age_metabolique. kcal: metabolisme_kcal. kJ: metabolisme_kj, only if no screen gives the kcal (don’t convert). Single number with no unit from 1 to 9 with the figure symbol: physique. Decimal number with no unit, about 15 to 45, with BMI: imc. bpm or a heart: fc_repos. Degrees (°): angle_de_phase. Number like 0.380 with ECW/TBW: ratio_eau_extracellulaire. If two values could match the same key and you can’t decide, write neither. 9. Arms, legs, trunk from a scale (on a Tanita: the screens from the two orange buttons, fat in % and muscle in kg): the right or left side is the one shown by the scale or the sheet. If you don’t know which segment it is, don’t write the line. A “percentage of normal” (InBody) is not a percentage of the segment: put it on an autre line. 10. Tape measurements, in cm: use the key with the side if it’s written, otherwise the key without a side. An arm circumference in cm is not arm muscle in kg. 11. Any other measurement shown with its name, one line each, in the format: autre: Exact name shown = value unit Don’t write as autre a measurement that already has its own key. 12. If you know which photos the values in a block come from, add the line photos: with their numbers, in the order of the list or of sending (example: photos: 1, 2, 3). Otherwise don’t write this line.
